notes:
Lead source: inbound signup (self-serve). POC started Feb trial credits. Primary contact: Maya Lin (Head of Product).

Summary:
- Early discovery: trial usage spiked for chat-support bot, now reporting latency spikes during peak hours. Mostly using hosted API from EU region but primary users are US-based.
- Business case: replace expensive human triage for Tier 1 support. Cost-sensitive; wants clear per-token estimates and regional guidance.

Technical details shared on call (2026-03-05 FF):
- Observed client-side p95 ~650ms on EU region for 512-token prompts; occasional 1.2s tails. US-west shows ~220-320ms for same workload.
- Using API default timeouts in client (10s) but frontend times out earlier at 6s causing partial responses.
- Prompt strategy: engineers concatenating full ticket history (avg 1.2k tokens) each call — big variance.
- No batching or prefix caching implemented; simple per-message calls.

AE notes / conversations:
- Maya: "We love the quality, but the users abandon when responses lag. Can we recommend best region and quick config changes?"
- Diego (SE) performed quick trace: upstream latency dominated by cross-region egress and long context lengths.

Recommendations provided (email 2026-03-07):
- Region guidance: route US traffic to us-west (lower median latency) and keep EU for EU customers. Consider multi-region fallback policy.
- Client timeout guidance: set frontend request timeout to 12s, backend to 20s for streaming fallbacks; avoid double timeouts.
- Prompt tuning: move to rolling-window context (truncate ticket history to last 300 tokens + condensed summary). Use embeddings for recall rather than full context when searching KB.
- Enable streaming and prefix/KV caching where applicable; recommend request-level batching for high-throughput periods.
- Cost tips: reduce max_tokens and lower sampling temp when deterministic answers OK; use shorter prompts and rely on post-processing for formatting.
